_install_instructions: templates/codex-hooks.json — User-installed Codex lifecycle hook template (two-step install).
STEP 1. Confirm Codex exposes PLUGIN_ROOT for plugin hook execution. The bundled
Cerberus hooks use PLUGIN_ROOT by default and CERBERUS_ROOT as an explicit
override for nonstandard installs.
STEP 2. Copy this JSON into Codex's hooks configuration file (typically
~/.codex/hooks.json or the platform equivalent — see docs/CODEX.md
§Configure Hooks for the exact target path) only if plugin-bundled hooks
are unavailable.
Example (POSIX shell):
cp templates/codex-hooks.json ~/.codex/hooks.json
Users who set CERBERUS_ROOT in their shell profile can point hooks at a
checkout root different from the installed plugin cache. The shared backend
reads CERBERUS_ROOT first via __cerberus_resolve_root, so this path is
supported without further changes.
OQ-Plan-3 / D48 RESOLUTION: Codex CLI 0.130.0 validates plugin-bundled hooks
resolving their installed root through ${PLUGIN_ROOT}. This template therefore
defaults to ${PLUGIN_ROOT} and keeps CERBERUS_ROOT as the explicit override.
This template registers SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit to keep the Codex
active-session registry fresh, plus Stop to enforce the review gate.
Claude-only team-automation lifecycle hooks are deferred to Phase 4 and are
not wired up here.

hooks.command: sh -c 'root="${CERBERUS_ROOT:-${PLUGIN_ROOT:-}}"; bin="$root/bin/cerberus"; [ -n "$root" ] || { echo "cerberus: plugin root not set" >&2; exit 127; }; command -v make >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "cerberus: make not found on PATH; install make and retry." >&2; exit 127; }; if ! make -q -C "$root" build >/dev/null 2>&1; then command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "cerberus: Go >= 1.22 not found on PATH; install Go and retry." >&2; exit 127; }; echo "cerberus: building... (this happens once after clone or upgrade)" >&2; start=$(date +%s); make -C "$root" build >&2 || exit $?; end=$(date +%s); echo "cerberus: build complete in $((end-start))s" >&2; fi; exec "$bin" hook codex-session-start'
